Hi Anne — quick technical notes on the SFTP flow (copied from our runbook):

• Push vs Pull: Redwood supports both SFTP push (client uploads to your host) and pull (Redwood pulls from your endpoint on a scheduled job). For nightly uploads we usually recommend push to minimize coordination.
• Temporary caching: for pull jobs we retain files in an encrypted staging area for up to 24 hours to allow processing retries; for push-only pipelines we do not retain copies beyond successful ingestion unless customers opt into log archival.
• Regional egress: if the SFTP host is in eu-west-1 and you want data to remain in-region, we recommend a private peering or using our Dedicated deployment; hosted routes may transit through a us-east-1 processing tier for orchestration metadata.

If StorGenius needs explicit SCCs or a UK Addendum, flag that now — otherwise we can include a standard EU-US transfer clause with the option to add SCCs on execution.

Laura

Can Redwood provide a subprocessors attestation (names + roles + data access level) at time of signing?

2) Transfers: we run in eu-west-1. We want either an express UK Addendum (in case of UK residents) or SCCs for EU-US transfers if any metadata is processed in the US. Can you indicate which transfer mechanism Redwood prefers for hosted customers?

3) E-sign: StorGenius prefers AdobeSign. If Redwood can send the final DPA via AdobeSign, please do so. If your DocuSign flow is automated and faster, we can accept DocuSign but would prefer AdobeSign.

Attached is our redline (high-level) with comments on subprocessor limitations and a request to limit log retention for auditable access.

- Transfers: for hosted customers Redwood's preferred default is the standard EU-US SCCs; we can include a UK Addendum if you expect a material UK resident population. We'll include SCCs in the initial execution copy unless you direct otherwise.
- E-sign: we can route the final DPA via AdobeSign for this contract. Please confirm the AdobeSign contact email for execution and we will create the envelope. If you prefer DocuSign instead for speed, reply and we'll use the DocuSign link.
